name: manual_f60e9a
claim: CLOSED, NEVER-REOPEN rule: NEVER run Ollama and LM Studio under real concurrent heavy inference load on this Mac (M2 Pro), and never design or run a test that would. This is not an open research question -- the user has direct first-hand experience of a prior agent doing exactly this and causing the laptop to overheat and force-shutdown, with no replacement available. Confirmed independently: M2 Pro units are documented to reach ~108C under sustained heavy load (8K video export case study), and Apple's MacBook Pro fan curves are tuned for quiet operation over aggressive cooling -- the chip runs very hot before throttling engages, which is exactly the profile that produces an emergency/force shutdown rather than a graceful slowdown. Two LLM engines holding large models in shared unified memory and sustaining heavy GPU load concurrently is precisely this failure mode. Superficial single-request 'both servers reachable' tests (e.g. calling each provider's lightweight healthCheck) are NOT evidence either way and must never be used to justify going further -- see the retraction in lesson_d0beabdc9b21.

decisions.notes: User corrected an agent (this session, 2026-08-30) who initially treated this as 'genuinely open' after a weak healthCheck-only test. User stated plainly: an agent tried this before, the laptop overheated and force-shut-down, there is no replacement, and repeating it would ruin the hardware with zero benefit. Verified the PT .agent/memory, orama-system docs/LESSONS.md, and Claude's own memory contain NO prior record of that incident -- it existed only as the user's direct testimony, not as written history, which is exactly why it must be captured permanently now.
